title: Infrastructure Will Define the Next Internet
partialText: The app-driven internet is hitting structural limits as platforms control data, real-time communication depends on single vendors, and scaling now requires geographic compliance. This article explores how decentralized real-time communication infrastructure (dRTC) changes those tradeoffs by distributing traffic, reducing vendor lock-in, improving resilience, and enabling AI-powered services closer to users.

title: Beyond Native Bots: Integrating Generative AI and Third-Party Intelligence into ServiceNow
partialText: ServiceNow's Virtual Agent is a capable conversation designer with solid integration into ITSM workflows. But it is fundamentally template-driven and relies on predefined conversation trees. Integrating tools like Moveworks, Glean Search, and X-Bot AI into the ServiceNow ecosystem does not just patch existing weaknesses.

title: The Risk Engineering Behind a 1 Million SKU Automated Pricing Engine
partialText: At massive scale, automated pricing becomes financial infrastructure. This architecture manages over 1 million SKUs and 500,000 daily updates using blast-radius containment, multi-phase validation, and exposure modeling to prevent systemic pricing failures. By separating optimization from risk enforcement and adding strict guardrails, the system reduced incidents from 3% to 0.1% while achieving 99.9% uptime.

title: Smart Tech, Passive Humans: The Psychology Behind Automated Living
partialText: Modern technology removes friction from daily life through automation, recommendations, and smart systems. While convenience improves efficiency, it can also distance people from responsibility and conscious decision-making. This article explores how frictionless design reshapes behavior, creating “behavioral pollution” where users passively rely on optimized systems instead of actively engaging with choices and consequences.

title: Passkeys in Symfony 7.4: How to Build a Completely Passwordless Future
partialText: Passkeys replace traditional passwords with cryptographic key pairs. Your device stores a private key, while the server only ever sees the public key. No fallback, no “reset password” links. Just pure, secure, biometric-backed passkeys.

title: 7 Iconic 20th-Century Ad Campaigns and What Today's Marketers Can Learn From Them
partialText: Some ads sell products; a rare few reshape culture. This article revisits seven iconic campaigns—Volkswagen’s “Think Small,” Nike’s “Just Do It,” Apple’s “1984,” and more—to show how simple, honest ideas created timeless marketing. Their success reveals a consistent pattern: the best campaigns don’t sell features, they sell identity, emotion, and belonging.

title: How to Build a Governance Layer for Claude Code With Hooks, Skills, and Agents
partialText: AI coding assistants don’t ignore instructions because they lack memory—they ignore them because compliance is optional. By adding lifecycle hooks, enforced Skill evaluation, structured commands, and specialist agents, developers can build a governance layer that ensures AI tools consistently follow repository rules and workflows. The result is dramatically improved reliability, safer tool usage, and AI assistants that behave more like disciplined engineering teammates than improvising interns.

title: A Practical Guide to Table Partitioning in PostgreSQL
partialText: As PostgreSQL tables grow into hundreds of millions of rows, query performance can suffer even with strong indexing. Table partitioning solves this by splitting a logical table into smaller physical partitions that PostgreSQL can scan selectively through partition pruning. This guide explains the three native strategies—range, list, and hash partitioning—and walks through real SQL examples for setting them up, indexing partitions, automating their creation, and managing data lifecycle efficiently. It also highlights common pitfalls, when partitioning actually helps, and when it adds unnecessary complexity.
